subject: Vendr + Whistic CAIQ fragment merge and evidence-tagging playbook
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudharbor.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Vendr/Whistic CAIQ fragments — canonical mapping help

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. We’ve started onboarding CloudHarbor to Vendr for evidence collection but we still maintain a Whistic profile with a partial CAIQ export from a previous engagement. The two portals have overlapping but non-identical CAIQ fragments (different question IDs and a few field name mismatches).

We need Redwood’s recommended approach for:
- reconciling CAIQ fragments so your portal view shows a single canonical response set (we’re flexible on whether to merge or keep fragments separate, but want guidance)
- tagging evidence with proof-of-possession (S3 presigned upload windows) and a manifest format you can consume
- minimizing duplication so downstream SIG/SOC2 reviewers see consistent answers

Attached: partial_caiq_export.zip (exports from Whistic + Vendr), access-logs-sample.csv (small sample of S3 presign logs).

Can we aim for next steps this week — a short playbook or checklist would be perfect.

Best,
Nina
Nina Patel
Head of Security Ops
CloudHarbor Inc.

---
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendr/Whistic CAIQ fragments — canonical mapping help

Hi Nina — thanks for the files, this is a common pattern when customers have multiple portal exposures. We’ll propose a short playbook and a minimal manifest spec to keep things deterministic for auditors. High-level plan: 

1) Triage + mapping (24–48h):
   - We’ll run a side-by-side diff of CAIQ question IDs and map alias names into a canonical column (we prefer preserving original fragments but adding a canonical_qid field so portal UIs can collapse).
   - For conflicting answers, we recommend a precedence rule: Vendor-provided signed attestation > Whistic export (older) > inferred defaults.

2) Evidence tagging + upload (3–5 days):
   - Provide a manifest.csv with rows: object_key, evidence_type, canonical_qid, source_portal, timestamp, checksum, proof_of_possession_token_id.
   - We’ll accept presigned PUT uploads to our ingest bucket; minimum presign window is 2 hours for bulk uploads but 24h is preferred to account for staging.

3) Post-ingest QA (2 days):
   - Automatic fingerprinting and dedupe; human audit for any conflicts flagged by the mapping rules.

Attached I’m dropping our evidence-ingest-playbook.pdf — it contains the manifest template and required metadata. Karthik will follow up with the presign manifest spec and the exact IAM permissions we need for a short-lived service account.

If that sounds ok we’ll schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the mapping rules and assign ownership. Proposed times: 2025-06-13 09:30 or 2025-06-13 15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendr/Whistic CAIQ fragments — canonical mapping help

Nina — quick technical follow-up from our side. For presign ingestion we need either:

A) A short-lived AWS IAM role (assume-role) that grants PutObject+PutObjectAcl on a staging prefix (preferred), or
B) A temporary service account with programmatic credentials that can call our presign endpoint (we will generate presigned PUTs for you).

Manifest requirements (sample row):
object_key,evidence_type,canonical_qid,source_portal,timestamp,checksum,proof_token_id
cloudharbor/20250612/ctl0.pdf,policy,CAIQ-02.1,Whistic,2025-06-12T08:32:00Z,sha256:abcd1234,ppt-9847

Notes:
- checksum must be sha256 hex.
- timestamp should be ISO-8601 UTC.
- proof_token_id is a short string we’ll return on successful presign that ties the S3 object to the ingested record.

I’ve attached presign-manifest-spec.md with the exact schema and examples. For the IAM approach we need a policy like:
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["s3:PutObject","s3:PutObjectAcl"],
    "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-evidence-ingest/cloudharbor/*"]
  }]
}

If you prefer we can handle upload orchestration — we’ll issue presigns and provide a short, auditable upload window.

– Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudharbor.com>

Subject: Re: Vendr/Whistic CAIQ fragments — canonical mapping help

Thanks Irene / Karthik — that plan looks good. We’ll provision a short-lived assume-role for the staging prefix and generate the manifest per your spec.

A couple quick Qs:
- For canonical_qid collisions (same semantic question but different CAIQ IDs), will Redwood annotate both source_qid values in the portal UI or collapse them into one visible question?
- Can we request a 24h presign window for the first bulk to avoid throttling on our side?

We can do the sync tomorrow at 15:00 PT. I’ll upload the temporary role ARN in a follow-up email and attach the initial manifest.

Appreciate the quick turn.
Nina
